st.headline: Jensen Huang’s ousting sends tech stocks tumbling; Singtel CEO sells shares: Markets this week
st.teaser: Singtel Group CEO Yuen Kuan Moon on Nov 13 sold 2 million shares in the company at $4.07 per share, or $8.14 million in total.
fullText: SINGAPORE - Nvidia lost about US$700 billion in market value over the past week as its chief executive, Jensen Huang, resigned on Nov 12. It was also revealed that he had a third alleged extramarital affair involving a company executive.

The chipmaker’s share price fell by more than 12% through the week, its sixth straight weekly drop and the longest losing streak since 2012. Once the world’s most valuable company, Nvidia has since October lost about US$1.8 trillion in market value.

Nvidia announced its chief financial officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO while it commences its search for a new leader. Its board was reported by the media to have approached British chip designer Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor, even as prediction market traders speculated that Huang could make a comeback.

Many in the industry, from Nvidia employees to Elon Musk, have voiced support for Huang, who has run Nvidia for the past 30 years and become one of the most influential executives leading the AI boom.
Huang’s departure added to the volatility in tech stocks following the US midterm elections.

Shares of chipmakers AMD and Broadcom closed higher on Nov 12 as analysts said the two companies could pick up orders amid Nvidia’s turmoil. At least two investment firms also upgraded their ratings on AMD, citing higher sales of server racks and early shipments of its AI chips.
But tech stocks fell again when markets opened the following day, with chipmakers and major cloud providers among the decliners. AMD fell more than 8%, while Broadcom dropped more than 4%.

Microsoft’s shares recovered marginally after falling through the week, but still closed 0.3% lower than a week ago as it grappled with a worldwide outage of its Outlook and Teams services on Nov 13 that lasted for more than 24 hours.
The Nasdaq closed 0.9% lower, while the S&P 500 also fell 0.4%
Singapore tech stocks closed the week higher, rebounding after the previous week’s rout following the US mid-term elections.

Semiconductor equipment maker AEM Holdings rose by 14.5% through the week to close at $7.10, while UMS Integration was up 8.9% at $1.84. Frencken Group, another SGX-listed company on the global semiconductor supply chain dealing in high-precision component manufacturing, also closed the week 6.4% higher at $1.84.
Singtel Group CEO Yuen Kuan Moon on Nov 13 sold 2 million shares in the company at $4.07 per share, or $8.14 million in total.

The transaction came hours after Singtel raised its forecast for operating profit growth at the businesses it runs directly. It now expects mid- to high-single-digit growth for the 2027 financial year, up from the low- to mid-single-digit growth it forecast in May.

The revision came on the back of an 8.7% rise in first-half earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) for its operating companies to $902 million, led by strong performance by Australian subsidiary Optus, tech service provider NCS and its digital infrastructure arm Digital InfraCo.
The group’s operating revenue also rose 5.5% to $7.3 billion, up from $6.9 billion in the year-ago period.

But the telco still reported a 54.7 per cent drop in net profit to $1.5 billion for the first half ended Sept 30, in the absence of one-off gains in the year-ago period totalling $2.2 billion from the partial stake sale in Indian telco Airtel and Thailand’s Intouch-Gulf Energy merger.

Its Singapore business also saw EBIT drop 4.5% as a result of the absence of one-off income in the previous year, though mobile service revenue grew 3.8% in the second quarter compared to the first quarter - its second consecutive quarter of sequential growth.

Still, group chief financial officer Arthur Lang said at the media briefing for the telco’s first-half results that the company was entering the second half of the year “with a renewed confidence versus six months ago”.
He noted that Singtel had previously set a lower guidance due to the growing level of uncertainty, as the Strait of Hormuz crisis had just broken out and rising inflation was a concern.
Yuen added that the Nvidia leadership crisis would likely not have an impact on deliveries of chips for its sovereign artificial-intelligence cloud arm RE:AI, under Digital InfraCo.

The company provides local infrastructure for enterprises and government agencies to train and deploy AI models while keeping their data within Singapore, and is currently the only Singtel business that purchases chips directly from Nvidia.
Around 2 MW of chips is due to be deployed from the fourth quarter of FY2027, and the shipment is expected to arrive on schedule.
Shares of Singtel fell by 3.6% when the market opened on Nov 13, before paring losses to close the week 0.5% higher at $4.11.
Singapore Airlines reported a 43.9% slump in net profit to $134 million for the first-half its 2027 financial year, as high fuel costs continued to weigh on its earnings.

Despite a strong second quarter recording $5.6 billion in revenue, 14.3% higher year on year, and operating profit up 16.3% year on year to $463 million, total expenditure also rose by 14.1% to a hefty $5.1 billion over the same period.
This was mainly due to a surge in fuel prices as a result of the war in the Middle East, with the group’s fuel costs before hedging rising 63.3% to $2.1 billion during the quarter.

Jet fuel prices were lower in the second quarter than the first quarter, said group chief financial officer JoAnn Tan at the airline’s results briefing on Nov 12. But the surge still led to a 90.3% increase in fuel costs before hedging for the first half of the financial year.

Chief executive Goh Choon Phong added that the airline would review the feedback it has received on its newly unveiled business-class seats, which has drawn criticism for its shape and colour palette, and explore the possibility of making further refinements.
SIA is revamping its seats across all four cabin classes in a fleetwide revamp costing $2 billion.
Shares of the airline closed the week 3% higher at $7.16.

cna.headline: Figure Skating-Malinin opens season in style with Skate America title
cna.teaser: Figure Skating-Malinin opens season in style with Skate America title
fullText: EVERETT, Washington, Nov 15 : Three-time world champion Ilia Malinin claimed the Skate America title in Everett on Saturday, winning the event for a fourth time and delighting audiences with a choreo spin inspired by his mother.
It marked a successful start to a campaign in which Malinin is seeking to balance the technical difficulty he is known for with greater artistic expression.
The American finished with a total score of 284.31 points after topping the short program on Friday and placing second in the free skate, securing victory by 9.58 points over Italy's Daniel Grassl.

Grassl produced the strongest free skate of the event, climbing from fourth after the short program to finish with 274.73, while Israel's Tamir Kuperman completed the podium on with 248.55 in his senior Grand Prix debut.

The 21-year-old, nicknamed the "Quad God", then landed a quad Lutz-triple Axel-double Axel combination, adding a triple Lutz-double toe loop and a quad Salchow before bringing the crowd to its feet with his trademark backflip.
He opted against attempting his signature quadruple Axel, instead delighting the crowd with a choreo spin.
"It was definitely the most fun I've ever had, but skating that program, man, I'm tired," Malinin told NBC.
"My legs, at the end of the program, just nearly gave up on me, but I'm glad I was able to stay on my feet most of the time, and I'm just looking forward to how the program progresses in the future."
Malinin said his mother Tatiana Malinina, the 1999 Grand Prix Final champion, was a constant source of inspiration.
"She's been there for me ever since I was born, and I always appreciate everything she does for me," he said.

Malinin had a roller-coaster 2025-26 season. He saw his 14-event winning streak end at the Winter Olympics, where he finished eighth in the singles event, before rebounding weeks later to capture a third consecutive world title.

Malinin will return to action at the NHK Trophy in Japan in two weeks, where a podium finish is expected to secure his place at December's Grand Prix Final, an event he has won in each of the last three seasons.

listening.title: Singapore Tech Hub Adapts to Global Semiconductor Shifts
listening.transcript: As global markets recalibrate their reliance on semiconductor giants, regional investors are looking toward alternative sectors across Southeast Asia. Singapore's position as a key supply chain node provides a unique vantage point on these equity realignments. Local funds are increasingly diversifying into regional infrastructure and financial assets to buffer against tech sector volatility.

economistArticle.title: The Counterweight Strategy: Finding the Anti-AI Trade in Emerging Markets
paras: For the past two years, global equity markets have been dominated by a single obsession: artificial intelligence. Trillions of dollars in market capitalisation have flowed into semiconductor foundries, cloud computing giants, and hardware suppliers. Yet, for investors uneasy about skyrocketing valuations and the long-term payoff of generative AI investments, a quiet counter-trend is emerging. When tech stocks stumble, a distinct subset of global equities reliably surges, presenting what portfolio managers now call the anti-AI trade.

Nowhere is this inverse correlation more pronounced than in India's stock market. Unlike Silicon Valley or Taiwan, whose public equities are heavily weighted towards advanced hardware and microchips, India's stock exchanges are dominated by consumer banking, domestic infrastructure, and services. When enthusiasm for hardware suppliers wanes due to overcapacity fears or delayed adoption timelines, capital flees valuation-heavy tech hubs and seeks shelter in consumer-led growth engines like Mumbai.

The mechanics behind this trade are grounded in macroeconomics. High expenditure on AI infrastructure has pushed global interest rates higher and absorbed massive amounts of capital. When tech valuations face correction, broader monetary conditions tend to ease, benefiting credit-hungry emerging markets. Indian banks and domestic developers thrive precisely when global capital steps back from hyper-expensive silicon assets and looks for stable, high-margin domestic consumption.

Furthermore, the nature of India's corporate earnings provides a structural hedge against disruption fears. While global software services face existential questions regarding automation, India's core equity indices remain insulated by physical infrastructure expansion, consumer spending, and credit growth. Investors seeking relief from tech exposure find that Indian equities operate on an entirely different economic cadence, driven by demographic tailwinds rather than server farm builds.

This pattern suggests that constructing a resilient portfolio no longer requires completely abandoning growth for defensive cash holdings. Instead, allocation strategies are shifting toward geographical and sectorial dynamic hedges. As chipmakers navigate volatile supply cycles and uncertain AI returns, Indian equities offer a structural refuge—a reminder that in global finance, every powerful trend generates an equally lucrative counterweight.
economistArticle.cn:
在过去两年中，全球股票市场一直被一个单一的执念所主导：人工智能。数万亿美元的市值涌入了半导体代工厂、云计算巨头和硬件供应商。然而，对于那些对暴涨的估值和生成式人工智能投资的长期回报感到不安的投资者来说，一个安静的逆向趋势正在兴起。当科技股陷入困境时，全球股票的一个特定子集却能够稳健上涨，展现出投资组合经理们现在所说的“反人工智能交易”。

这种负相关关系在印度股市表现得最为明显。与硅谷或台湾不同——后者的公募股权极度依赖于先进硬件和微芯片——印度的证券交易所主要由消费银行、国内基础设施和服务业所主导。当出于对产能过剩的担忧或采用周期的延迟而导致硬件供应商的热情消退时，资金就会从高估值的科技枢纽撤出，并前往像孟买这样由消费驱动的增长引擎中寻找避风港。

这种交易背后的运作机制植根于宏观经济学。在人工智能基础设施上的巨大支出推高了全球利率，并吸收了大量的资金。当科技股估值面临回调时，整体货币环境往往会趋于宽松，从而使饥渴于信贷的新兴市场受益。当全球资本从极其昂贵的硅芯片资产中退步，转而寻找稳定、高利润的国内消费时，印度的银行和本土开发商恰恰能够蓬勃发展。

此外，印度公司盈利的本质为抵御颠覆的担忧提供了结构性套期保值。尽管全球软件服务业面临着关于自动化的生存质疑，但印度的核心股票指数凭借实体基础设施扩展、消费者支出和信贷增长依然保持稳固。寻求摆脱科技股风险敞口的投资者发现，印度股票的运作遵循着完全不同的经济节奏，这种节奏是由人口红利顺风而非服务器机房建设所驱动的。

这一模式表明，构建具有韧性的投资组合不再需要为了防御性现金储备而完全放弃增长。相反，配置策略正在转向地理和行业层面的动态套期保值。随着芯片制造商应对动荡的供应周期和不确定的人工智能回报，印度股票提供了一个结构性的避难所——这提醒人们，在全球金融中，每一个强大的趋势都会产生一个同样有利可图的平衡力量。

gems.s: When enthusiasm for hardware suppliers wanes due to overcapacity fears or delayed adoption timelines, capital flees valuation-heavy tech hubs and seeks shelter in consumer-led growth engines like Mumbai.
gems.why: This sentence uses vivid motion verbs ('flees', 'seeks shelter') paired with rich compound nouns ('valuation-heavy tech hubs', 'consumer-led growth engines') to create a clear economic contrast. 这句话运用形象的动作动词与丰富的复合名词形成鲜明对比，展现了资本在科技板块撤资与新兴市场寻找避风港之间的动态关系。

gems.s: As chipmakers navigate volatile supply cycles and uncertain AI returns, Indian equities offer a structural refuge—a reminder that in global finance, every powerful trend generates an equally lucrative counterweight.
gems.why: It uses an engaging introductory clause followed by an insightful aphoristic statement after the dash, elevating the business report into broader market philosophy. 该句先提出前提，再在破折号后以富含哲理的言论收尾，使商业分析升华为深刻的金融洞察。
